text:
Sam: Quick follow-up from the precision RFC — I propose we centralize the per-request precision decision in the orchestration layer instead of embedding heuristics in the runtime. Thoughts?
Jess: +1 to centralizing, but what about rollback safety and visibility? We need clear telemetry for quality regressions. :thinking:
Kai: Centralization helps routing decisions (region/cost/latency) but watch out for prefix/KV cache effects — switching precision mid-conversation can invalidate caches and spike latency.
Maya: Agreed. Proposal for API contract: client can optionally send a `precision_hint`, orchestration returns `precision_choice` and `fallback_policy`. Runtime receives only exec flags. Example:```json
{
  "user_hint": "prefer_fp8",
  "orchestration_decision": "int8_with_requant",
  "fallback": "gradual_requant_then-fp16"
}```
Sam: Nice. That keeps runtime simple. Also suggests we keep determinism: runtime should never make autonomous downgrade decisions except when instructed by orchestration.
Andrew: Concern: enterprise customers will want per-tenant overrides (SLA/quality). How do we let them pin precision or opt out without complicating routing?
Maya: Per-tenant policy could be a higher-priority rule in the orchestrator policy engine. We already have routing tiers; just plumb a `tenant_precision_override` field in the decision layer.
Jess: Telemetry we need: per-decision: `decision_id`, `precision_before`, `precision_after`, `deg_score`, `latency_p50/p95`, `kb_cache_hit_rate`. These let us detect regressions tied to a decision.
Kai: For cache invalidation, add `kv_cache_stability` flag. Orchestration can avoid precision switches for ongoing sessions where `kv_cache_stability == low`.
Sam: Operational fallback playbook suggestion: if deg_score > threshold for X minutes, orchestrator auto-rolls back that precision profile for affected routes and creates Ops ticket. Keep human-in-the-loop for cust-specific rollbacks.
InfraBot: canary run results: "canary-precision-orch-v1" completed: 10k requests, avg latency +3ms, deg_score median 0.02, 12 failures (investigating).
Andrew: Investigating failures — are they correlated with longctx or certain prompt shapes? If so we should add a prompt-shape guard.
Maya: We need a compact decision payload shape for orchestrator->runtime so we don't bloat RPC. Proposal:```yaml
precision_decision: "int8_requant"
quality_budget_id: "qb_2026_05_01"
decision_id: "d-1727778888-01"
kv_cache_action: "invalidate_partial"
```
Jess: Also include `stability_ttl` (how long to keep this decision for a session). Defaults: 10min for chat flows, 30s for ephemeral requests.
Kai: Runtime change minimal: accept flags {precision, requant, kv_cache_action, decision_id}. If decision_id seen again, reuse cached kv state.
Sam: Ops checklist for rollout: 1) policy engine tests, 2) shadow canaries, 3) perf and degscore dashboards, 4) per-tenant opt-out gating, 5) rollback/runbook doc.
Andrew: One more: legal/compliance — document audit trail for decisions (decision_id, who/what triggered) for Private customers.
Maya: I'll draft the boundary API and runbook this week. Will add sample telemetry queries for `deg_score` baselining.
Jess: Thanks. If we keep orchestration responsible for decisioning, it centralizes policy + audit. :+1:
Sam: Ok I’ll update the RFC with the orchestration-first flow and small runtime flag contract. Reviewing notes: avoid frequent intra-session switches, surface decision IDs to telemetry, per-tenant overrides in policy engine, explicit fallback policies.
Kai: Quick note — test matrix: (short prompt vs longctx) x (fp8/int8/4bit) x (kv_cache_stability high/low). We should run synthetic and production shadowing.
InfraBot: remind: playbook template PR created at https://git.internal/redwood/precision-orch-playbook/pull/42
Maya: tagging folks for review: @Jess @Kai @Andrew — will send draft link in 30m.
Andrew: Thanks all.
Sam: End of thread — action items captured.
